sentences.text: The single known species, Polarornis gregorii, was found on Seymour Island, Antarctica, in Late Cretaceous rocks dated to about 66 million years ago.
Sankar Chatterjee first announced the discovery of Polarornis gregorii in 1989 but did not officially describe and name the species until 2002.

Polarornis is classified as a prehistoric bird that is either a possible member of the family Vegaviidae or the group Aequornithes. A 2025 study by Irazoqui and colleagues recovered Polarornis as a member of Aequornithes, with one analysis grouping it with Gaviidae. The parent group of the genus Polarornis is the family Vegaviidae.
Polarornis lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Gerald Mayr criticized the original description of the fossils, noting that Polarornis differed from loons in important characteristics and that the specimen's completeness was overstated.
